questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Practicing and studying in French and living in a unique city which is relevant to the field I study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, we received an email of when to meet up for a big welcome day for exchange students, where we met the other students arriving from DK, got the student card, and got some general information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: On the first week there was a meeting with the Erasmus coordinator in person, who was very helpful in answering our questions, also later on. This was reassuring as prior to arrival, communication with the general study administration was not the best with several unanswered mails and calls.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult, though I guess it's also a question of luck. The university provided a list of links of where to search for accommodation, and there are private agencies out there that can help to find short-term leases (but these are more expensive). I would try to arrive to Paris some time before starting the semester and go to viewings in person, it was difficult to search remotely.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive. It can be a bit isolating to live far away from uni and friends, but good for exploring the city as a local.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My friends staying in university dorms were satisfied and this is a lot more affordable option, it is worth applying for.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out a paper during the first meeting with the Erasmus coordinator. The course catalogue for the semester however was not published until the last week of August, meaning my pre-approval application with KU was based on the outdated list of courses. So I had to redo the pre-approval application, which required some extra time and effort. However it all turned out fine in the end. The good thing about course registration is that it was possible to change/de-register from courses at Sorbonne for the first few weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The previous years' course catalogue was on the uni's website which helped to make the pre-approval application. The Erasmus coordinator managed the process on Sorbonne's end and answered questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This went smoothly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a very different system from KU and it can seem confusing, but don't stress over it - it's all gonna work out when you get there in person.  If you want to take courses in other disciplines than your own, dedicate time to exploring this option during the first week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was not enough available modules in art history to reach the 30 ECTS that were expected by KU, so I decided to supplement my selection with an archeology class. The workload that I ended up having this way was more challenging than what I was used to, with having several physical classes every day, several of them lasting until 9 pm. To have enough credits therefore I ended up following a combination of courses that were quite unrelated to each other, the topics spanning from antiquity to contemporary and being very detailed, also requiring quite a lot of assignments at once in the end. For me it was challenging to follow this wide combination of topics, times and cultures. Thinking back I would consider looking into courses at the same faculty but outside art history and would only choose a few art history courses that I would want to specialise in.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All the art history courses tackled very specific topics and were quite detailed and advanced. All courses were taught in French.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Totally different. The classes consisted predominantly of lectures with no or very little discussion following up. Instead of reading and independent work, emphasis is put on very thorough note taking of what the professor says in class (and memorising it for most evaluations). Most courses gave a very 'factual' presentation of the studied topic going into the smallest details, but often with no critical examination following up on what we heard. Certain aspects of some courses were poorly organised; sometimes classes would be cancelled without notifying students; or it would be unclear how Erasmus students will be evaluated until quite late in the semester, or slides were not shared. That being said I still enjoyed some courses. In my perception, the syllabus for art history is more 'up to date' at KU but Sorbonne is good at providing a very solid ground of knowledge in specific topics, so in a way they complete each other. While I gained a lot of new knowledge, I found the top-down teaching style challenging, and I left questioning the value of this type of encyclopedic knowledge today.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Patrimoine : histoire, théorie, législation, institutions, collections ; Archéologie romaine ; Art contemporain 1 ; Art contemporain XXe-XXIe s. ; Art moderne 1 ; Spécifique d'art contemporain ; Projet professionnel: entretien avec des professionnels

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend 'Art contemporain XXe-XXIe s.' and 'Spécifique d'art contemporain' as they were the most clearly structured courses, taught by engaged professors who also aimed at sparking discussions in the classroom.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Neutral as I did not attend any through the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were French language classes for foreign students, as well as sports clubs and public lectures, film club... There is a student organization in charge of almost weekly social gatherings for Erasmus students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attending social events for Erasmus students is an easy way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's Paris, there is always something exciting to do! There is also quite a few castles with parks in the proximity of Paris, which can be interesting as there is not a lot of nature inside the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy as I already spoke the language quite well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: That can be difficult. There were not really any social spaces in the art history institute, so my best advice is to just start talking to the people you sit next to before or after classes - people were quite curious to meet foreign students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The hierarchies when addressing any ‘superior' (teacher, senior people) can be challenging when coming from DK - a lot of formal politeness is expected in these situations. I also found bureaucracy unnecessarily complicated.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture, the city, the unique arts & culture scene of Paris

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Explore the option of taking courses outside your discipline
2. Be prepared that the teaching style is very different from KU
3. Use your time in Paris well - you can actually go and see a lot of the material you learn about if in art history or a related field, the city is a massive resource

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: More about living in Paris: there is a great and cheap public bike system which I was happy to use. Also with your student card you can get a warm meal at the CROUS canteens for 4 EUR.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a unique city, making new friendships and polishing my French language skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating the different teaching style.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
